request: Split the two jobs `governs:` currently serves in the memory schema. It is the staleness witness (staleness.mjs — narrow means less churn) AND the path leg scoped memory filters on when deciding which entries surface at a phase (scoped-memory.mjs:43 — narrow means fewer readers reached). One field, opposite pressures, so an entry whose evidence and audience differ cannot be scoped correctly for both. Candidate shape (the spec decides): an additive frontmatter field for surfacing scope that defaults to `governs:` when absent, leaving every existing entry and every consumer install unchanged. Acceptance criteria are driven by the four entries that still churn and cannot be narrowed today. Continues the in-flight `stale-keying-and-glob-scope` workflow; the splitter extraction and four narrowings already landed under the quickfix track and the spec expands onto them.
novelty_evidence: Searched .claude/memory for an existing entry naming the staleness-vs-surfacing conflict in `governs:` and found none — the closest, tests-glob-restales-nine-entries-on-every-test-edit-4c7a, records the CHURN symptom only and prescribes narrowing, which is what turned out to be unsafe for one of its own nine. No spec under docs/specs/ covers the memory frontmatter schema. The fix adds a new frontmatter field, which has no in-repo precedent. The conflict itself is measured, not inferred: churn moved 9 of 9 -> 4 of 9 and all four remaining are blocked by it, and the PATH_LEG_BASELINE comments record the inverse failure at 5f52ba2 where the repair was to WIDEN an entry that 'surfaced at zero phases for a new writer added under hooks'.
track_reason: Upgraded from tdd-quickfix (the leanest track, and the one this workflow started on) because the root-cause fix is a shipped-contract change: it adds a field to the memory frontmatter schema that every consumer install must tolerate, and it changes which entries surface at which phase. A quickfix carries no spec and no gate A, so the change would ship unreviewed. Upgrading ADDS the human approval rather than routing around it. Re-triaged mid-flight on 2026-08-27 with the engineer's explicit approval.

prior_track.reason: Root cause found mid-execution; see track_reason.
landed_before_retriage: New Foundation module .claude/hooks/lib/memory-entries.mjs owning stripFrontmatter, entryKeyFromHeading, splitFlatEntries. Four readers repointed (sweep.mjs, memory_session_start.mjs, shape.mjs) and their private copies deleted. Byte-exactness preserved for sweep's replaceBlock/deleteBlock write path, which locates a block by text.indexOf and silently no-ops on a miss.
splitBlocks first-word keying fixed — the flat-store index now names an entry by its whole heading, matching sweep.

The known-key guard now applies to sharded reads, so an entry's own `## ` sub-section is no longer minted as a separate entry. Limit recorded: a flat store has no external key list, so the naive split remains there.
Four governs: narrowings applied via applyNarrowing with body bytes, scope, verified-at and last-touched verified unchanged.

One narrowing REVERTED: grep-reports-no-match-on-utf8-files-it-calls-binary. Narrowing it stopped it surfacing on .claude/** where it has recurred four times. That revert is the worked example the spec argues from.
prior_track.spec_treatment: This work is CONTEXT for the spec, never retro-fitted acceptance criteria. Writing ACs to describe code already written is rubber-stamping. The spec's ACs cover the unwritten split only.

expected_failures.check: audit-baseline manifest hash drift, and the 15 tests that shell out to it
expected_failures.reason: This landing edits three manifest-pinned baseline files (memory_session_start.mjs, sweep.mjs, shape.mjs) and adds one new module (hooks/lib/memory-entries.mjs). obj/template/.claude/manifest.json is stamped by scripts/build-template.sh, which takes no stage argument and rewrites the entire shipped tree — too large a diff to carry through the TDD loop, where it would also inflate the right-size gate measure and the review diff.
expected_failures.measured: 15 of 3496 tests as of 2026-08-27, every one tracing to the single stale sha256 for .claude/skills/memory-sync/shape.mjs. Scoped and full audit both exit 1. Zero non-audit failures.
expected_failures.verify_tick_protocol: test.cmd is `audit && node --test`, so the audit leg short-circuits the suite. For this workflow's verify ticks run `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` directly and record the audit leg as deferred. This is a NAMED, time-bounded suppression with an owner, not a muted alarm — the distinction the a-check-that-measured-nothing-reports-success landmine turns on.
expected_failures.discharge_check: Run scripts/build-template.sh, then `node .claude/skills/audit-baseline/audit.mjs` SHALL exit 0 and the full suite SHALL be green under the unmodified test.cmd. An audit still red at integrate is a real failure and not this debt; do not carry this entry past integrate under any circumstances.
expected_failures.discharge_evidence: scripts/build-template.sh restamped the manifest; the UNMODIFIED test.cmd (audit && node --test) exits 0 with 3510 tests, 3494 pass, 0 fail. The verify-tick override in project_conventions was not used: the suite is honestly green, so no leg was skipped and the four-line stamp needs no caveat. obj/template/.claude/hooks/lib/memory-entries.mjs ships and is hashed.
